symptom: On Podman-on-Windows, the devcontainer that `mxcli init --container-runtime podman` generates fails postCreateCommand after the mxcli download succeeded: `chmod +x ./mxcli` errors on the workspace bind mount, and every container start re-downloads the binary
cause: postCreateCommand ended in an unguarded `chmod +x ./mxcli`, which a mount that does not honour Unix modes rejects, failing the whole command. Its fast path, `file ./mxcli | grep -q Linux`, never matched because the generated image did not install `file`
insight: A generated shell one-liner has two failure modes that no Linux CI run shows: a step that is fatal only on a foreign filesystem (a Windows bind mount ignores chmod), and a guard that silently never fires because its tool is missing from the image. Assert both on the generated text: every chmod on the mounted workspace is tolerant, and every command a guard runs is installed by the Dockerfile the same generator writes
